- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.30) or neutral — model fails to account for downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 75+), producing exaggerated highs that fail to correct quickly — apply lagged mean reversion to dampen peaks.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating 0.30 and 0.70), model overfits short-term noise — reduce forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-5 day moving average.
- Forecast horizon 30d often misses mean reversion to 70–73 range — adjust downward bias if sentiment is weak or price is above 74.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.20–0.30) over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope — avoid steep upward trends.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment decay — if sentiment drops below 0.30, reduce forecast growth rate by 15–20%.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling (e.g., 75+ with -0.30 sentiment), model overcorrects — forecast should be slightly below peak, not flat.
